cases.name: diamond_reverse_decl_order
cases.description: Classic diamond: d=b+c, b=a*2, c=a+10, a=base+1. Declared in REVERSE topo order (d first, a last) so a naive declaration-order evaluator gets all NaN/wrong.
cases.notes: Correct eval order is a,b,c,d. Single-pass must equal fixpoint. base=4 -> a=5, b=10, c=15, d=25.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: wide_fanin_seven_chained
cases.description: One field sums 7 derived fields each of which derives from base. Wide fan-in (7 deps) declared before its dependencies. Stresses in_degree=7 resolution.
cases.notes: total has in_degree 7; g=10 -> each pX=10+X, total=7*10+(1..7)=70+28=98.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: wide_fanout_one_to_six
cases.description: One derived root (root) feeds 6 independent consumers. Wide fan-out: 6 fields share in_degree 1 on root, all become ready simultaneously, lexicographic tie-break.
cases.notes: root=16; c1=15,c2=32,c3=4,c4=116,c5=256,c6=4. ^ is power, sqrt(16)=4. Order-independent among c1..c6.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: two_independent_components
cases.description: Two completely separate DAG components in one schema (x-chain and y-chain share no edges), interleaved in declaration. Both must order correctly independently.
cases.notes: Two disjoint components. ax=2->x1=3->x2=9; ay=9->y1=7->y2=12. Interleaved declaration order.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: deep_linear_chain_reversed
cases.description: Deep 6-deep linear chain f<-e<-d<-c<-b<-a<-base, declared fully reversed (f first). Naive evaluator would fail every level; only correct topo order works.
cases.notes: base=0 -> a=1,b=2,c=3,d=4,e=5,f=6. Strict linear chain, order must be a..f.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: mixed_regular_and_chain
cases.description: Some derived fields depend only on regular fields (no edges, in_degree 0) mixed with a chain that depends on them. r_only is ready immediately; chained depends on it.
cases.notes: r_only depends only on regular reg1 -> in_degree 0. reg1=3->r_only=6; reg2=4->mid=10; chained=6*10=60.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: diamond_with_extra_tail
cases.description: Diamond (top->a,b; a,b->mid) PLUS a tail field that fans in mid AND one diamond arm. Lexicographic tie-break between two ready arms must hold.
cases.notes: seed=5->top=10; a=11,b=9; mid=99; tail=99+11+9=119. a and b ready together, tie broken lexicographically.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: cross_component_shared_leaf
cases.description: Two derived consumers (sumAB, sumBC) overlap on a shared middle field b, forming a non-tree DAG. b has fan-out 2; a,c each used once. Non-obvious order.
cases.notes: k=6 -> a=7,b=12,c=18; sumAB=19, sumBC=30. b shared by both sums.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: interleaved_three_diamonds
cases.description: Three diamonds sharing one common base, all fields declared in scrambled (non-topological) order. Stresses determinism of Kahn across many simultaneously-ready nodes.
cases.notes: base=1->core=10. l1=11,r1=9,d1=20; l2=12,r2=8,d2=96; l3=13,r3=7,d3=20. Many ready at once, lexicographic order.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: fanin_after_fanout
cases.description: root fans out to 3 mids, then a single sink fans those 3 mids back in. Combined fan-out then fan-in diamond, declared sink-first.
cases.notes: in0=3->root=9; m1=10,m2=11,m3=12; sink=33. Sink in_degree 3.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: chain_referencing_earlier_derived_skip
cases.description: Field z references both a deep ancestor (a) AND a near parent (y), skipping levels. Diamond-ish skip edge. a must order before y and z; y before z.
cases.notes: p=4->a=5; x=10; y=x+a=15; z=a+y=20. z and y both skip-reference a.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: lex_order_nonmonotonic_keys
cases.description: Topological order differs from lexicographic key order: dependency forces 'zfirst' to evaluate before 'aafter'. Catches evaluators that sort keys alphabetically instead of topologically.
cases.notes: Topo order zfirst(=11) then aafter(=22). Alphabetical 'aafter' first would NaN. seed=10.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: self_loop_only_valid_nan
cases.description: Pure self-reference a=a+1. Per line 53 the self-edge is stripped, so validator treats it as VALID (in_degree 0). At runtime a is not a context var when evaluated -> meval Errs -> NaN -> NULL. This deliberately contradicts the prompt's naive claim that self-ref is a cycle.
cases.notes: Validator-VALID (self-edge subtracted at line 53, in_degree 0, eval_order assigned). At runtime evaluates to NaN -> NULL because 'a' is a derived field never inserted as a context var before its own eval. No device_values needed (no regular fields). || UPDATED for DP1 fix: the validator now rejects any key referenced in its own formula with FORMULA_SELF_REFERENCE (a 1-node cycle). The old behavior (accepted, then permanent NULL at runtime) was the DP1 bug.
cases.review_note: updated 2026-06-10: DP1 fixed — self-reference now rejected at validation.

cases.name: two_node_mutual_cycle
cases.description: Classic 2-node cycle a=b+1, b=a+1. Each depends on the other derived field, both in_degree 1, neither ever reaches queue -> order incomplete -> CIRCULAR with both keys sorted.
cases.notes: unresolved = {a,b}, sorted -> error string 'FORMULA_CIRCULAR_DEPENDENCY:a,b'. No unknown vars (a and b are both field keys).
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: four_node_long_cycle
cases.description: Long cycle a->b->c->d->a. a=b, b=c, c=d, d=a. Every node in_degree 1, queue starts empty, nothing resolves -> all four unresolved -> CIRCULAR.
cases.notes: unresolved sorted -> 'a,b,c,d'. Pure cycle with no entry point; Kahn queue is empty from the start so order stays size 0.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: cycle_embedded_among_valid_dag
cases.description: A 2-node cycle (x=y+1,y=x+1) buried among many valid derived fields that form a clean DAG plus regular fields. A buggy detector that resolves the easy valid ones might miss the embedded cycle. Validator must still report ONLY the cyclic keys.
cases.notes: Valid fields p,q,r,s resolve fine (len(order)=4); only x,y are unresolved (len(deps)=6 != 4). unresolved sorted -> 'x,y'. raw_a/raw_b are regular and add no edges. No UNKNOWN_VARS (all referenced ids are field keys). Tests that valid DAG nodes do not mask the embedded cycle.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: near_miss_diamond_dag_valid
cases.description: Looks tangled by name (multiple fields cross-referencing) but is actually a valid diamond DAG: d depends on b and c, both depend on a. No cycle. Must be VALID. Lulls a name-based heuristic into thinking it is cyclic.
cases.notes: Diamond DAG a->{b,c}->d. eval_order: a=0, then b,c (tie, lexicographic b<c), then d last. base=10: a=11, b=22, c=33, d=55. Numeric oracle should agree both ways.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: self_and_others_in_cycle
cases.description: Field references ITSELF and another field, where the other completes a cycle: a=a+b, b=a+1. The self-term a in a's formula is stripped at line 53, but the cross edge a<->b (a needs b, b needs a) still forms a 2-node cycle.
cases.notes: deps[a] = {a,b} - {a} = {b}; deps[b] = {a}. Mutual cycle a<->b. unresolved sorted -> 'a,b'. Confirms self-term removal does NOT hide a genuine cross-cycle. || UPDATED for DP1 fix: the literal self-term in 'a = a + b' now trips FORMULA_SELF_REFERENCE:a before Kahn cycle detection runs (still a rejection, earlier and more precise).
cases.review_note: updated 2026-06-10: DP1 self-ref check fires first; cross-cycle would still be caught by Kahn.

cases.name: self_loop_plus_regular_valid
cases.description: Self-reference that also reads a regular field: a = a + r. Self-edge stripped, regular field adds no edge -> in_degree 0 -> VALID. Runtime still NaN because a is unavailable in context at its own eval.
cases.notes: Validator-VALID: deps[a] = {a,r} - regular{r} - {a} = {} -> in_degree 0 -> eval_order 0. Runtime: 'a' missing in ctx -> meval Err -> NaN -> NULL. Both oracles converge to NaN/NULL. result is NULL regardless of r. || UPDATED for DP1 fix: the validator now rejects any key referenced in its own formula with FORMULA_SELF_REFERENCE (a 1-node cycle). The old behavior (accepted, then permanent NULL at runtime) was the DP1 bug.
cases.review_note: updated 2026-06-10: DP1 fixed — self-reference now rejected at validation.

cases.name: two_disjoint_cycles
cases.description: Two independent cycles in one schema: a<->b and c<->d, no shared nodes. All four unresolved -> CIRCULAR lists all four sorted.
cases.notes: deps a={b},b={a},c={d},d={c}. in_degree all 1 -> queue empty -> order empty. unresolved={a,b,c,d} sorted -> 'a,b,c,d'.
cases.review_note: ok — no node has in_degree 0; queue starts empty; all four unresolved.

cases.name: tail_into_cycle_valid_prefix
cases.description: Valid tail t=m+1 (m regular) resolves; then a=b+t, b=a+1 form a cycle. Only a,b unresolved; t is fine.
cases.notes: deps t={} (m regular), a={b,t}, b={a}. in_degree: t=0, a=2, b=1. t resolves -> a drops to 1, still needs b; b still needs a. unresolved={a,b} sorted -> 'a,b'. t NOT in unresolved.
cases.review_note: ok — verified t drains (in_degree 0), a/b remain in the b<->a cycle. unresolved excludes t.

cases.name: three_node_cycle_with_chord
cases.description: 3-node SCC a->c, b->{a,c}, c->b with an extra chord (b also depends on a). All three unresolved.
cases.notes: deps a={c}, b={a,c}, c={b}. in_degrees a=1,b=2,c=1 -> queue empty. unresolved={a,b,c} sorted -> 'a,b,c'.
cases.review_note: ok — re-derived in_degrees (a=1,b=2,c=1); no zero-degree node; all unresolved.

cases.name: near_miss_reverse_name_order_valid
cases.description: Valid DAG where dependency direction runs opposite to lexicographic key order (z<-y<-x). Clean chain, VALID, despite src declared after its users.
cases.notes: deps x={} (src regular), y={x}, z={y,x}. Kahn: x=0, y=1, z=2. src=4 -> x=8, y=9, z=17. Partitioning is key-based so declaration order is irrelevant. Valid.
cases.review_note: ok — confirmed acyclic; eval_order x=0,y=1,z=2; src has device value.

cases.name: long_cycle_one_valid_sink_outside
cases.description: 5-node cycle a->b->c->d->e->a plus a non-cyclic sink w=a+1 that depends on a cycle member. w never resolves, so unresolved set includes w too.
cases.notes: Cycle {a,b,c,d,e} never drains (all in_degree 1, queue empty). w depends on a (derived) -> in_degree[w]=1 never reaches 0. unresolved = deps.keys()-order.keys() = {a,b,c,d,e,w} sorted -> 'a,b,c,d,e,w'. Reported set is the topo leftover, which includes non-cyclic-but-dependent w.
cases.review_note: ok — verified queue starts empty (no in_degree-0 node), so order={} and ALL six (incl. w) are unresolved.

cases.name: uvf_pure_constant_no_vars
cases.description: Formula of only numeric constants/operators (no identifiers). No vars to be unknown -> passes -> finite number.
cases.notes: c has truthy formula -> derived. regular_keys={}, all_keys={c}. _extract_formula_vars finds no identifiers -> unknown={}, deps[c]={} -> eval_order 0. result 13. No regular fields, device_values={} correct.
cases.review_note: ok — confirmed regex finds zero identifiers; sole derived field; valid eval to 13.

cases.name: uvf_references_regular_only_valid
cases.description: Derived field references only a regular field. Regular fields add no edge and are always known; valid eval.
cases.notes: raw in all_keys -> no UNKNOWN_VARS. deps[scaled]={raw}-regular{raw}-{scaled}={} -> eval_order 0. raw=7 -> result 75.
cases.review_note: ok — verified deps[scaled] empty; raw covered by device_values.

cases.name: uvf_missing_field_reference
cases.description: Formula references an identifier that is neither a field key nor an allowed function. Classic unknown-var error.
cases.notes: vars={a,ghost}; all_keys={a,d}; ghost not a key/function -> FORMULA_UNKNOWN_VARS:d:ghost.
cases.review_note: ok — ghost confirmed unknown; key in message is the offending derived field 'd'.

cases.name: uvf_typod_function_name
cases.description: Typo'd function name sqrtt(x). Validator treats unknown function-looking tokens as variables -> sqrtt is unknown var -> error.
cases.notes: UPDATED for DP6(a) fix: the parser distinguishes call targets from variables. 'sqrtt(' is a function call of a non-whitelisted name -> FORMULA_UNKNOWN_FUNCTION:r:sqrtt (previously misreported as an unknown VARIABLE).
cases.review_note: updated 2026-06-10: parser-based validation; call target -> UNKNOWN_FUNCTION.

cases.name: uvf_multiple_unknown_sorted
cases.description: Several unknown identifiers; probes that unknown set is sorted and comma-joined.
cases.notes: vars={zeta,alpha,ok,mu}; all_keys={ok,m}; unknown={alpha,mu,zeta} sorted -> FORMULA_UNKNOWN_VARS:m:alpha,mu,zeta.
cases.review_note: ok — sorted unknown set confirmed (alpha,mu,zeta); ok is a known regular key.

cases.name: uvf_field_named_like_function_log_hidden
cases.description: Regular field literally named 'log' (an allowed function name) and formula 'log + 1'. Function-name exclusion strips 'log' from vars: validator passes but runtime treats log as a function call -> NaN.
cases.notes: UPDATED for DP3/DP9: 'log' is not a meval builtin at all (whitelist fixed), and the parser treats a bare identifier as a VARIABLE regardless of name collisions (meval Var/Func namespaces are separate). 'log + 1' with log=100 -> 101, stored as 101 — the old 'runtime NULL' expectation reflected a harness model error (DP9).
cases.review_note: updated 2026-06-10: field usable; expected value 101, not NULL.

cases.name: uvf_field_named_min_unreferenceable
cases.description: Regular field named 'min' referenced in another formula. 'min' is whitelisted, so the token is dropped -> validator never sees it as a var; the field is effectively un-referenceable.
cases.notes: UPDATED for DP9: a bare 'min' (not followed by '(') is a VARIABLE in meval; with the parser-based extraction the dependency on field 'min' is tracked and the runtime reads the device value: min=9 -> z=18. The 'unreferenceable' claim was REFUTED against real meval 0.2 (DP9).
cases.review_note: updated 2026-06-10: field IS referenceable; expected 18, not NULL.

cases.name: uvf_known_funcs_not_vars
cases.description: Formula uses several whitelisted functions on a real var. None of the function names count as unknown vars; valid eval.
cases.notes: tokens sqrt,abs,exp removed as functions; only var {x} which is known. valid. x=16 -> 4 + 16 + 1 = 21.
cases.review_note: ok — all three names are exact whitelist members and excluded; only x remains, known.

cases.name: uvf_substring_of_function_name
cases.description: Identifiers 'sq' and 'sqr' that are substrings/prefixes of 'sqrt' but not the exact token. They are real unknown vars -> error. Probes exact-match (not substring) exclusion.
cases.notes: regex finds {sqr,sq,x}; exclusion is exact-match so sqr,sq stay; not field keys -> unknown={sq,sqr} sorted -> FORMULA_UNKNOWN_VARS:w:sq,sqr.
cases.review_note: ok — confirmed substring tokens are not excluded; both unknown.

cases.name: uvf_function_name_with_suffix
cases.description: Token 'log10' (looks like a function but only 'log'/'log2' are whitelisted). 'log10' treated as unknown var -> error.
cases.notes: UPDATED for DP3/DP6(a) fix: 'log10(' is a call of a non-whitelisted function (meval has neither log nor log10) -> FORMULA_UNKNOWN_FUNCTION:q:log10.
cases.review_note: updated 2026-06-10: parser-based validation; call target -> UNKNOWN_FUNCTION.

cases.name: uvf_first_derived_unknown_wins
cases.description: Earlier derived field (source order) has an unknown var, later one is valid. Unknown-var check iterates derived in source order -> earlier field's error fires.
cases.notes: derived=[(1,bad),(2,good)] in source order; 'bad' hit first -> FORMULA_UNKNOWN_VARS:bad:nope. 'good' valid but never reached.
cases.review_note: ok — verified iteration over `derived` is source order; bad precedes good.

cases.name: uvf_unknown_in_chained_derived
cases.description: Derived field references a valid earlier derived field plus an unknown identifier. Derived keys count as known; stray unknown still errors.
cases.notes: all_keys={src,mid,top}; mid known (derived). vars for top={mid,phantom}; phantom unknown -> FORMULA_UNKNOWN_VARS:top:phantom. (mid checked first is valid: src known.)
cases.review_note: ok — mid passes (src known); top fails on phantom. all_keys includes derived keys.

cases.name: uvf_underscore_and_digits_ident
cases.description: Formula references a snake_case identifier with digits that is NOT a field key. Confirms regex captures full [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* token and flags it unknown.
cases.notes: temp_2b is one valid identifier, not a field key, not a function -> FORMULA_UNKNOWN_VARS:calc:temp_2b. v1 is known. Verified against validator.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: div_by_zero_positive_inf
cases.description: Positive numerator over a device-supplied zero denominator. IEEE f64 gives +inf; to_sql_literal maps it to 'Infinity'.
cases.notes: 5/0 -> +inf -> 'Infinity'. Oracle must use f64 division (numpy/Rust), NOT Python '/' which raises ZeroDivisionError. || UPDATED for new engine semantics: +/-Infinity now maps to SQL NULL (to_sql_literal treats ALL non-finite as NULL) and is not fed into the meval ctx.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: div_by_zero_negative_inf
cases.description: Negative numerator over zero denominator yields -inf, mapping to '-Infinity'.
cases.notes: -3.5/0 -> -inf -> '-Infinity'. Confirmed via numpy f64. || UPDATED for new engine semantics: +/-Infinity now maps to SQL NULL (to_sql_literal treats ALL non-finite as NULL) and is not fed into the meval ctx.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: zero_over_zero_nan_null
cases.description: Both numerator and denominator zero -> 0/0 is NaN in IEEE f64 -> NULL column.
cases.notes: 0/0 -> NaN -> NULL. Both oracles converge on NaN.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: sqrt_negative_nan_null
cases.description: sqrt of a negative device value -> NaN -> NULL. Uses allowed function sqrt.
cases.notes: sqrt(-16) -> NaN -> NULL. f64::sqrt of negative is NaN (numpy confirms), not an error.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: overflow_to_inf
cases.description: Multiplying a near-max-double magnitude by 10 overflows to +inf -> 'Infinity'.
cases.notes: 1e308*10 > f64 max -> +inf -> 'Infinity'. Oracle must use f64 multiply; numpy confirms inf. || UPDATED for new engine semantics: +/-Infinity now maps to SQL NULL (to_sql_literal treats ALL non-finite as NULL) and is not fed into the meval ctx.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: negative_overflow_to_neg_inf
cases.description: big^2 overflows to +inf, then 0 - inf = -inf via the ^ power op. Confirms ^ is POWER and overflow direction.
cases.notes: big^2 = 1e400 -> +inf; 0 - inf = -inf -> '-Infinity'. WARNING for harness: Python's 1e200**2 raises OverflowError; oracle MUST use f64 power (numpy.power) which returns inf. Verified inf/-inf via numpy. || UPDATED for new engine semantics: +/-Infinity now maps to SQL NULL (to_sql_literal treats ALL non-finite as NULL) and is not fed into the meval ctx.
cases.review_note: ok; added explicit harness warning that Python ** overflows here while meval/numpy f64 yield inf.

cases.name: pythagorean_power_op
cases.description: x^2 + y^2 using ^ as exponentiation (NOT xor). Finite valid result, checks power-op faithfulness.
cases.notes: 3^2 + 4^2 = 25 (finite). ^ is POWER in meval; a Python oracle must use ** not ^ (xor). No inf/NaN.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: subtractive_cancellation
cases.description: Catastrophic cancellation: (a+1) - a where a is huge loses precision; result is 0 not 1.
cases.notes: 1e17+1 not distinct from 1e17 in f64, so (a+1)-a == 0.0, not 1. Confirmed 0.0 in Python f64. Both oracles agree.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: chain_inf_propagates_finite
cases.description: Intermediate derived field becomes +inf (div by zero); a later derived field references it; inf propagates through arithmetic.
cases.notes: UPDATED for new engine semantics: step1 = 2/0 -> +inf which is now NON-FINITE -> SQL NULL and NOT fed into ctx; step2 references missing step1 -> Err -> NULL. Infinity no longer propagates into the DB (DP4 fix).
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: chain_nan_cascade
cases.description: Intermediate derived field is NaN (0/0); a downstream field references it -> NaN poisons arithmetic.
cases.notes: bad = 0/0 -> NaN. Rust: NaN is a successful eval (Ok), so bad=NaN IS inserted into ctx (main.rs 885-887); downstream = NaN*2+7 = NaN -> NULL. Both fields NULL. eval_order: bad=0, downstream=1 (verified).
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: inf_minus_inf_nan
cases.description: Two +inf intermediates subtracted: inf - inf is NaN in IEEE -> NULL. Indeterminate form through chaining.
cases.notes: UPDATED for new engine semantics: infA=1/0 and infB=2/0 are +inf -> NULL each, not fed to ctx; indet references missing vars -> Err -> NULL. All three stored NULL.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: tiny_underflow_to_zero
cases.description: Multiplying two tiny magnitudes underflows to exactly 0.0 (finite, not NaN/inf).
cases.notes: 1e-200 * 1e-200 = 1e-400 < smallest subnormal -> underflows to +0.0. SQL literal '0'. Confirmed 0.0 via numpy f64.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: apparent_power_pf_chain
cases.description: 3-level derived chain: apparent power S from P,Q; power factor PF from P,S (chains on derived S); pf_pct from PF. Stresses multi-hop chaining through eval_order.
cases.notes: S=100, PF=0.8, pf_pct=80. eval_order apparent_power_kva=0 < power_factor=1 < pf_pct=2 (verified). ^ is POWER.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: pf_zero_load_div_zero_nan
cases.description: No-load: P=Q=0 so apparent_power_kva=0, then power_factor = 0/0 = NaN -> NULL. Probes 0/0 IEEE path on an idle-meter snapshot.
cases.notes: apparent_power_kva=0 (valid). power_factor = 0/0 -> NaN -> NULL. eval_order apparent=0 < power_factor=1. Both oracles converge to NaN.
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: voltage_current_averages
cases.description: Flat per-phase averaging: voltage_avg and current_avg each from three regular phase fields. No derived-derived edges; output is order-independent.
cases.notes: voltage_avg=231, current_avg=12. Both derived have in_degree 0, but eval_order is a global counter so they get DISTINCT values: lex tie-break gives current_avg=0, voltage_avg=1 (verified against validator). Values are order-independent since both depend only on regular fields.
cases.review_note: Fixed factually wrong note: original claimed 'both get eval_order 0'. The validator assigns a global incrementing idx, so the two independent in_degree-0 fields get 0 and 1, not both 0; lex tie-break yields current_avg=0, voltage_avg=1.

cases.name: voltage_unbalance_max_min_avg
cases.description: Voltage unbalance % using max()/min() over phases and chaining on derived voltage_avg. Probes 2-arg max/min plus a derived dependency.

fields.formula: (max(max(voltage_l1, voltage_l2), voltage_l3) - min(min(voltage_l1, voltage_l2), voltage_l3)) / voltage_avg * 100

cases.notes: voltage_avg=231, spread=6, unbalance=6/231*100. voltage_unbalance_pct depends on derived voltage_avg -> eval_order voltage_avg=0 < voltage_unbalance_pct=1 (verified).
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: reverse_declared_order_topo
cases.description: Derived fields declared in REVERSE dependency order (consumer before producer) to force topo reorder. apparent listed last but must eval first. Probes eval_order vs source order.
cases.notes: S=130, PF=120/130, pf_pct=PF*100. Source order is consumer-first; Kahn yields eval_order apparent_power_kva=0 < power_factor=1 < pf_pct=2 (verified, matches forward-declared case).
cases.review_note: ok

cases.name: energy_delta_per_phase_power
cases.description: Mixed realistic derivations: total energy from three phase counters, per-phase power V*I, and total power summing derived per-phase powers (chain). Stresses fan-in where one derived depends on three other derived fields.
cases.notes: Verified against validator. Four in_degree-0 derived (energy_import_total_kwh, power_l1_w, power_l2_w, power_l3_w) get eval_order 0..3 by lexicographic tie-break; power_total_w depends on the three powers -> eval_order 4 (NOT 1). power_total_w = 230*10+231*20+229*30 = 2300+4620+6870 = 13790; energy_import_total_kwh = 6000.875.
cases.review_note: ok structurally; corrected note: power_total_w eval_order is 4 (lexicographic tie-break orders the four ready fields first), not 1 as originally claimed.

cases.name: circular_pf_apparent_cycle
cases.description: Erroneous spec: apparent_power_kva defined in terms of power_factor AND power_factor in terms of apparent_power_kva. True 2-node cycle among derived fields -> FORMULA_CIRCULAR_DEPENDENCY.
cases.notes: Verified: validator raises FORMULA_CIRCULAR_DEPENDENCY:apparent_power_kva,power_factor (unresolved sorted). active_power_total_kw is regular so adds no edge. No device_values needed (never reaches eval).
cases.review_note: ok — confirmed exact message via validator run.

cases.name: typo_unknown_phase_var
cases.description: Formula references current_l4 which does not exist (only l1..l3 wired). Probes FORMULA_UNKNOWN_VARS on a realistic phase-count typo.
cases.notes: Verified: FORMULA_UNKNOWN_VARS:current_avg:current_l4. Fires before topo sort.
cases.review_note: ok — confirmed exact message via validator run.

cases.name: self_ref_running_energy_accumulator
cases.description: TRAP: engineer writes energy_accumulated = energy_accumulated + energy_delta_kwh expecting an accumulator. Validator does NOT flag self-reference (self-edge stripped at line 53) -> VALID, but at runtime energy_accumulated is not yet a ctx var -> eval Err -> NaN -> NULL.
cases.notes: Verified validator-VALID (pure self-edge stripped at line 53 -> in_degree 0 -> eval_order 0). At runtime energy_accumulated references itself before it is inserted into ctx -> meval Err -> NaN -> NULL. Both oracles converge to NaN/NULL. cases.name: duplicate_key_phantom_cycle
cases.description: A chain where a derived field key (s1) is declared twice. The standalone validator has NO duplicate detection; the second s1 OVERWRITES deps[s1], and because s1 and s2 then point at each other, a phantom 2-node cycle is created -> FORMULA_CIRCULAR_DEPENDENCY (NOT FIELD_KEY_DUPLICATE).
cases.notes: REWRITTEN. Original expected FIELD_KEY_DUPLICATE, which is a ROUTER-level check in create_schema (line 114-115) and is NEVER raised by the target validator _validate_and_order_derived_fields. Empirically the validator processes both s1 entries; the second formula (s2+1) overwrites deps[s1]={s2}, while deps[s2]={s1}, forming a 2-node cycle. Verified output: FORMULA_CIRCULAR_DEPENDENCY:s1,s2. all_keys dedupes via set() so no UNKNOWN_VARS. This is a genuine adversarial probe of how a duplicate key silently corrupts the dependency graph in the validator. || UPDATED for DP6(d) fix: the validator now has its own duplicate-key guard (defense-in-depth for import/Store entry points), so the dup is rejected as FIELD_KEY_DUPLICATE:s1 before the phantom cycle can form.
cases.review_note: updated 2026-06-10: DP6(d) fixed — validator-level duplicate detection added.

CORRECTION to original author: eval_order is NOT all 0; Kahn pops one at a time incrementing idx, so with lexicographic tie-break eval_order is da=0,db=1,dc=2,dd=3,de=4. Result is still fully order-independent because there are NO inter-derived edges. Verifies regular-field deps add NO edge.

The validator assigns distinct eval_orders 0..4 via Kahn's idx increment (lexicographic tie-break: da,db,dc,dd,de). Output remains order-independent. Confirmed VALID via standalone run of the actual validator logic; numeric outputs unchanged. Also corrected description's '10 derived fields' -> actual count is 5.
